content: Just a heads up to everyone working on category theory in mathlib, more precisely everyone that uses the category instance on types: I will merge #36613 when CI passes. This refactor makes the morphisms in the category of types a structure (implementation detail: it is actually a doubly nested one-field structure), to introduce an API barrier between morphisms in Type and plain functions. This is exactly what we do for the other concrete categories, and after this is merged, the concrete category API will be usable in Type as well. If you run into issues with your PRs breaking, I'm happy to help fix them. Usually this will be very straightforward. To promote a function f to a morphism, you just write TypeCat.ofHom f, or use the notation ↾f (which already existed in mathlib but was rarely used, this arrow is generated by \upr in VSCode). Like in other concrete categories, there is a coercion from morphisms to functions. Some of the specialized API for the category of types has been deprecated in favour of more general constructions that work in concrete categories, e.g. FunctorToTypes.map_comp_apply is now Functor.map_comp_apply, works for all concrete categories and is generated with @[elementwise] on Functor.map_comp.
(coming here from bumping FLT): note that the ↾ notation is scoped: open scoped TypeCat to get it. And thank you Dagur for announcing this here or else I would have been completely bewildered!
That notation used to be scoped in the CategoryTheory namespace, maybe we want to change it back?
#38655 scopes the notation in CategoryTheory and replaces TypeCat.ofHom with the notation throughout mathlib
Is there anything in that namespace? There is quite a lot in CategoryTheory.Limits.Types, is that what you meant?
https://loogle.lean-lang.org/?q=%22CategoryTheory.Types%22 shows a few hits, but also renaming CategoryTheory.Limits.Types to CategoryTheory.Limits.TypeCat would make sense to me
Ah, it seems to be mostly instances in CategoryTheory.Types
Just TypeCat would be better than CategoryTheory.Limits.TypeCat IMO. Something with limit/colimit usually appears after the namespace anyway. That way, it's more like TopCat.limitCone, etc

Christian Merten said:

and a few declarations related to docs#CategoryTheory.Types.jointlySurjectivePrecoverage

I see. That should be TypeCat.jointlySurjectivePrecoverage, right? Without the CategoryTheory.
It would be nice to also fix the naming of docs#CategoryTheory.typesGrothendieckTopology while we are at it.
